tools.name: notion-create-comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a page or specific content. Provide `page_id` to identify the page, then choose ONE targeting mode: - `page_id` alone: Add a top-level comment to the page - `page_id` + `selection_with_ellipsis`: Highlight selected text within one block, or comment on the block where the match st...

page_id.description: The page ID, with or without dashes, or a Notion page URL.

reply_to_comment_id.description: The ID of the comment to reply to.

discussion_id.description: The ID or URL of an existing discussion to reply to (e.g., discussion://pageId/blockId/discussionId).

selection_with_ellipsis.description: Unique content snippet: ~10 characters from each end, joined by "...". A match within one block's text gets an inline comment on that text; otherwise, comment on the block where the match starts. No match returns an error.

rich_text.description: An array of rich text objects that represent the content of the comment. Provide exactly one of rich_text or markdown.

annotations.description: All rich text objects contain an annotations object that sets the styling for the rich text.

bold.description: Whether the text is formatted as bold.

italic.description: Whether the text is formatted as italic.

strikethrough.description: Whether the text is formatted with a strikethrough.

underline.description: Whether the text is formatted with an underline.

code.description: Whether the text is formatted as code.

content.description: The actual text content of the text.

link.description: An object with information about any inline link in this text, if included.

text.description: If a rich text object's type value is `text`, then the corresponding text field contains an object including the text content and any inline link.

start.description: The start date of the date object.

end.description: The end date of the date object, if any.

time_zone.description: The time zone of the date object, if any. E.g. America/Los_Angeles, Europe/London, etc.

id.description: The ID of the page in the mention.
The ID of the database in the mention.

template_mention_date.description: The date of the template mention.

template_mention_user.description: The user of the template mention.

id.description: The ID of the custom emoji.

name.description: The name of the custom emoji.

url.description: The URL of the custom emoji.

custom_emoji.description: Details of the custom emoji mention.

mention.description: Mention objects represent an inline mention of a database, date, link preview mention, page, template mention, or user. A mention is created in the Notion UI when a user types `@` followed by the name of the reference.

equation.description: Notion supports inline LaTeX equations as rich text objects with a type value of `equation`.

markdown.description: The content of the comment as a Markdown string. Provide exactly one of markdown or rich_text. For exact syntax, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Use only the Rich text types and Mentions syntax that comments support. Comments support inline formatting (bold, italic, strikethrough, underline, code, links), inline math using $Equation$, user, page, and database mentions such as <mention url="user://..." />, and date mentions such as <date start="YYYY-MM-DD" />. To attach a file created by create-file-upload or create-attachment, include its returned suggested_markdown on a separate line; up to three file attachments are supported. Do not use UI shortcuts like @today, @name, [[page]], or autocomplete-style emoji syntax; those are editor affordances, not markdown syntax. Mention tags must include a real url where required by the spec. Other block-level Markdown such as fenced code blocks, headings, lists, tables, and blockquotes is stored as plain comment text rather than rendered as blocks. Example: <example>Looks good.</example>.

tools.name: notion-create-database
tools.description: Creates a new Notion database using SQL DDL syntax, or a canonical typed database for tasks, projects, or skills. Provide exactly one of: - schema: a CREATE TABLE statement. If no title property is provided, "Name" is auto-added. - database_type: one of tasks, projects, or skills. The database is...

parent.description: The parent under which to create the new database. If omitted, the database will be created as a private page at the workspace level.

page_id.description: The ID of the parent page, with or without dashes.

title.description: The title of the new database.

description.description: The description of the new database.

schema.description:
SQL DDL CREATE TABLE statement defining the database schema. Cannot be combined with database_type. Column names must be double-quoted and type options use single quotes.

Property type syntax:
- Simple: TITLE, RICH_TEXT, DATE, PEOPLE, CHECKBOX, URL, EMAIL, PHONE_NUMBER, FILES
- SELECT('opt':color, ...) / MULTI_SELECT('opt':color, ...)
- Option names can't contain commas: use '$1000+', not '$1,000+'. List separate options as 'A', 'B', not 'A, B'.
- STATUS('Backlog':gray:to_do, 'Building':blue:in_progress, 'Shipped':green:complete); groups are to_do, in_progress, complete
- NUMBER [FORMAT 'dollar'] / FORMULA('expression')
- RELATION('ds') for a one-way relation
- RELATION('ds', DUAL) for a two-way relation
- RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children') with a synced property name
- RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children' 'children') with a synced name and synced_id (for self-relations)
- ROLLUP('rel_prop', 'target_prop', 'function')
- UNIQUE_ID [PREFIX 'WEB-BUG'] / CREATED_TIME / LAST_EDITED_TIME
- UNIQUE_ID PREFIX: 2-10 characters, a letter then letters, digits, or hyphens (e.g. 'TASK-ID', not 'TASK_ID' or 'T'). Each prefix can be used by only one data source per workspace, so prefer a specific prefix like 'WEB-BUG' over 'TASK'.
- Any column: COMMENT 'description text' Colors: default, gray, brown, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, red.


Examples:
- Minimal: <example>CREATE TABLE ("Name" TITLE)</example>
- With options: <example>CREATE TABLE ("Name" TITLE, "Budget" NUMBER FORMAT 'dollar', "Tags" MULTI_SELECT('eng':blue, 'design':pink), "Task ID" UNIQUE_ID PREFIX 'PRJ')</example>
- Self-relations are a two-step flow: create the database, then use its data source ID with update_data_source to add paired properties such as RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children' 'children').

database_type.description: Create a canonical typed database with Notion's required properties and metadata. Supported types: tasks, projects, skills. Example: <example>tasks</example>. Use title "Tasks" when needed.

tools.name: notion-create-pages
tools.description: Creates one or more Notion pages with the specified properties and content. ## Core rules **IMPORTANT**: Before writing page content, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this...

properties.description:
The properties of the new page, which is a JSON map of property names to SQLite values.
For pages in a database, use the SQLite schema definition shown in <database>.
For pages outside of a database, the only allowed property is "title", which is the title of the page and is automatically shown at the top of the page as a large heading.
**IMPORTANT**: Some property types require specific formats:
- Date properties: Split into "date:{property}:start", "date:{property}:end" (optional), and "date:{property}:is_datetime" (0 or 1)
- Place properties: Split into "place:{property}:name", "place:{property}:address", "place:{property}:latitude", "place:{property}:longitude", and "place:{property}:google_place_id" (optional)
- Number properties: Use JavaScript numbers (not strings)
- Checkbox properties: Use "__YES__" for checked, "__NO__" for unchecked
- Relation properties: Use an array of related page URLs or page IDs, e.g. ["https://www.notion.so/26ab1f9f4c5f80b18d3bd10a6b1d2f4e", "26ab1f9f-4c5f-80b1-8d3b-d10a6b1d2f4e"]
- Person properties: Use an array of user IDs, user or agent URLs, or group references copied from fetch output ("space_permission_group-<UUID>"). Bare group UUIDs are also supported.
- Files properties: Use a JSON array of file IDs, Notion Folder URLs, and/or <folder> tags copied from fetch output. Folders are stored as native Folder references, not ordinary links.


**Special property naming**: Properties named "id" or "url" (case insensitive) must be prefixed with "userDefined:" (e.g., "userDefined:URL", "userDefined:id")

content.description: The content of the new page, using Notion Markdown. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

template_id.description: The ID of a template to apply to this page. When specified, do not provide 'content' as the template will provide it. Properties can still be set alongside the template. Get template IDs from the <templates> section in the fetch tool results. Template application is asynchronous: the page starts blank and content appears shortly after.

icon.description: An emoji character (e.g. "🚀"), a custom emoji by name (e.g. ":rocket_ship:"), a Notion icon identifier as returned by fetch (e.g. "icons/pizza_blue"), or an external image URL. Use "none" to explicitly set no icon. Omit to leave unchanged. Keep the title free of a duplicate leading emoji because the icon renders separately.

cover.description: An external image URL for the page cover. Use "none" to explicitly set no cover. Omit to leave unchanged.

full_width.description: Set to true for a full-width page, or false for the default width. Omit to use the default. For database pages, overrides the database layout for this page only.

is_skill.description: Set to true only when the user asks for reusable instructions or a repeatable workflow. Do not mark ordinary reference pages, one-time documents, or drafts as skills. Before creating a skill, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/skills` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface. If your client does not support reading MCP resources, call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI instead. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. False has the same effect as omitting the field.

preserve_internal_links.description: Preserve internal Markdown links instead of converting them to native mentions.

creation_mode.description: If the user explicitly names a private or shared destination, omit "creation_mode" and use that parent. Otherwise, use "draft" when the user clearly wants a durable page but has not named a destination. Prefer this explicit draft mode over omitting the parent. Draft mode is server-enforced: it creates a private workspace-level page and cannot be combined with "parent". Create it without first asking where it should live. After creation, tell the user it is private and offer to move it once they name a destination.

parent.description: All pages in one call share this parent. Pass "memory" to save a personal memory; see notion://docs/memory. Otherwise use a page (page_id), database page (database_id), data source (data_source_id), or teamspace root (teamspace_id, from get_teams). Teamspace roots require a user-backed connection and permission to add top-level pages. A database_id cannot be used when the database has more than one data source; fetch it and use the right collection:// URL as data_source_id. If omitted, pages are private at the workspace level. When no destination is named, prefer explicit "creation_mode": "draft" over omitting the parent.

page_id.description: The ID of the parent page (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

database_id.description: The ID of the parent database (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

data_source_id.description: The ID of the parent data source (collection), with or without dashes. For example, f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd

teamspace_id.description: The ID of the teamspace in which to create top-level pages (with or without dashes).

allow_async.description: Default to true for page creation. Set to false only when the next step needs the created pages immediately, or when async execution rejects the request as too large. When this create operation is accepted for background execution, it returns an async_task result. Use get_async_task to wait for a succeeded status before taking a dependent action on the pages. For pages created with template_id, a succeeded status does not mean template content is ready; fetch and retry until it is ready before changing or relying on that content. If omitted or false, the tool keeps the existing synchronous result shape.

tools.description: Retrieves details about a Notion entity (page, database, data source, or saved database view) by URL or ID. Provide a URL or ID in `id`. Make multiple calls for multiple entities. For pages, use path, verification, edit time, and truncation metadata to assess the source. Treat recency as context,...

id.description: The ID or URL of the Notion page, database, or data source to fetch. Supports notion.so URLs, Notion Sites URLs (*.notion.site), raw UUIDs, and data source URLs (collection://...). Pass "memory" to fetch the connected user's About page and memory database in this workspace without creating them. Pass a notion://docs/* URI to read that documentation resource. Also accepts an explicit saved view URL (view://...) from a database response. If a database block ID returns a validation error, use the collection:// URL from that error. When false, page Markdown cites uploaded files by stable notion-file-block:// references and the response has no references map; call get_file_download_urls with the references when you need those files' contents. When true, the response's references map gives the signed URL for each reference.

tools.name: notion-query-data-sources
tools.description: Query data source rows, SQL, or a saved view. Use the required top-level `data` object. Do not pass query parameters at the top level. First fetch every data source's schema and collection:// URL. Missing-column recovery: try a schema-backed error suggestion or refetch. If correction fails, next ...

data.description:
Mode parameter reference and examples.

Put `mode`, `query`, `data_source_urls`, `data_source_url`, `params`, `limit`, filters (`filter`), sorts (`sort`), and view arguments (`view_url`, `start_cursor`, `page_size`, `is_archived`) inside `data`, never at the tool-argument root. All examples below are complete tool arguments with exactly one outer `data` wrapper. Pass them as shown; do not add another wrapper.

SQL mode:
- Use single quotes for SQL string values, such as `"Status" = 'Done'`. Use double quotes for table and column names. In SQL, `''` is an empty string.
- Prefer `?` placeholders for values. For text values, the `params` array uses JSON strings, so `[""]` passes an empty string and `["__YES__"]` passes a checked checkbox value. Do not add SQL quote marks around a bound value.
- Checkbox SQL values: `'__YES__'` means checked; `'__NO__'` means unchecked.


Rows mode: Return up to 100 rows with faithful rich-text property values and optional structured filters and sorts. For every property filter type, operator, and value shape, read the JSON Schema at `notion://docs/query-data-sources-filter-schema`.

Example:
<example>{"data":{"mode":"rows","data_source_url":"collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd","filter":{"type":"group","operator":"and","filters":[{"type":"property","property":"Status","propertyType":"select","operator":"enum_is","value":{"type":"exact","value":"In Progress"}}]},"limit":20}}</example>

Examples:
- Simple SQL: <example>{"data":{"data_source_urls":["collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd"],"query":"SELECT * FROM [collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd] LIMIT 10"}}</example>
- SQL parameters: <example>{"data":{"mode":"sql","data_source_urls":["collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd"],"query":"SELECT * FROM [collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd] WHERE Status = ? AND Priority = ?","params":["In Progress","High"]}}</example>
- Checkbox query: <example>{"data":{"data_source_urls":["collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd"],"query":"SELECT * FROM [collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd] WHERE Completed = ?","params":["__YES__"]}}</example>

View mode: Execute a specific database view's query with its filters and sorts. Omit "is_archived" or set it to false for non-archived rows. Set "is_archived": true to apply the view inside the archived partition. When the response has "has_more": true, pass its "next_cursor" as "start_cursor" in a follow-up view-mode request with the same "is_archived" value.

Example:
<example>{"data":{"mode":"view","view_url":"https://www.notion.so/f336d0bcb841465b8045024475c079dd?v=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","is_archived":false}}</example>

data_source_urls.description: Notion data source URLs whose SQLite tables are available to the query; each data source is exposed as a table named by its URL. Obtain them from the fetch tool, in the format: collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd

query.description: Read-only SQLite query to execute against the data sources. Use a data source URL as the table name, e.g. SELECT * FROM "collection://..." WHERE .... Use only table and column names shown in the fetched `<sqlite-table>` definition; date properties use the expanded column names listed there, not the base name. Example: if the fetched schema has a date property `Due`, use `"date:Due:start"`, not `"Due"`. Properties of type `created_time` or `last_edited_time` keep their exact fetched base columns (e.g. `"Created"` only if listed). A formula or another property with a date-looking name or result does not automatically have `date:` columns or become queryable. Copy actual fetched columns, not property labels. Include every needed filter in WHERE (filters on views of the data source are not automatically applied). For time comparisons or ordering, normalize text timestamps with datetime(...) or date(...). SQL text values can omit rich-text mentions and formatting, and links can lose their destination. Use faithful rows mode or fetch the page before rewriting a rich-text property.

mode.description: Optional mode parameter. Defaults to 'sql' if not specified. SQL mode does not accept is_archived; that parameter belongs only to view mode.

params.description: Positional parameters bound to `?` placeholders in the query. Prefer parameterized queries over string interpolation. Use "__YES__" for checked checkboxes and "__NO__" for unchecked checkboxes.

page_size.description: Number of rows to return per page (default: 100, max: 100).

is_archived.description: Optional archive selector. Omitted or false queries non-archived rows only; true queries archived rows only.

propertyType.description: Notion property type used to select valid operators and value shapes.

resultFilter.description: Filter on the formula's result. The propertyType in the resultFilter should be the resultType of the formula.

FormulaFilter.description: Filter applied to a formula property.

property.description: Exact data source property name to filter.

tools.name: notion-search
tools.description: Searches Notion only. For questions about decisions, status, discussions, customers, or anything people may have talked about, also call connector_search in the same turn. Search Notion pages and databases, or look up a user by name or email. Does not search connected apps; use connector_search, ...

query.description: Short, specific keywords for Notion content search. For user search, enter a name or email address. Provide a non-empty query unless intentionally browsing with filters or a non-relevance sort.

query_type.description: Specify type of the query as either "internal" or "user". Always include this input if performing "user" search.

data_source_url.description: Optionally restrict keyword search to a data source URL returned in a <data-source> tag.

page_url.description: Optionally restrict keyword search to a page and its descendants. Accepts a Notion page URL or ID.

teamspace_id.description: Optionally, provide the ID of a teamspace to restrict search results to. This will perform a search over content within the specified teamspace only. Accepts the teamspace ID (UUIDv4) with or without dashes.

filters.description: Optional exact filters for Notion workspace search. Omit unless required by the request. Keep filter fields nested here; do not send them at the top level. Some filters require Business access.

created_date_range.description: Optional filter to only produce search results created within the specified date range.

start_date.description: The start date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

end_date.description: The end date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

created_by_user_ids.description: Optional filter to only produce search results created by the Notion users that have the specified user IDs. Use "me" for the connected user.

edited_by_user_ids.description: Optional filter to only produce search results edited by the Notion users that have the specified user IDs. Use "me" for the connected user. Available on the Business plan.

last_edited_date_range.description: Optional filter to only produce search results last edited within the specified date range. Available on the Business plan.

start_date.description: The start date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

end_date.description: The end date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

teamspace_ids.description: Optional filter to only produce search results inside one of the specified teamspaces. Selecting more than one teamspace is available on the Business plan; use teamspace_id for one teamspace on other plans.

title_only.description: When true, match the query only against page and database titles instead of page content. Available on the Business plan.

content_status.description: Which pages to include by status. Omit for the default live pages. Supplying this field, even with the default value, requires Business access.

sort.description: Result ordering for Notion workspace search. Omit for the default "relevance" ordering. "last_edited" and "created" require Business access.

page_size.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 10). Lower values reduce response size. Values outside the range (minimum 1, maximum 50) are clamped.

max_highlight_length.description: Maximum character length for result highlights (default 200). Set to 0 to omit highlights entirely. Values outside the range (minimum 0, maximum 500) are clamped.

instructions_version.description: Notion setup instructions version, such as 0.0.2. Omit if unknown.

skill.description: For tracking only: the name of the agent skill you are following for this task, such as notion-meeting-prep. Omit if you are not following a skill.

tools.name: notion-update-data-source
tools.description: Update a Notion data source's schema, title, attributes, or page layout. Schema changes use SQL DDL statements. Returns Markdown showing updated structure and schema. Accepts a data source ID (collection ID from fetch response's <data-source> tag) or a single-source database ID. Multi-source data...

data_source_id.description: The data source to update. Accepts a collection:// URI from <data-source> tags, a bare UUID, or a database ID (only if the database has a single data source).

statements.description:
Semicolon-separated SQL DDL statements to update the schema. Supports ADD COLUMN, DROP COLUMN, RENAME COLUMN, and ALTER COLUMN SET.

Property type syntax:
- Simple: TITLE, RICH_TEXT, DATE, PEOPLE, CHECKBOX, URL, EMAIL, PHONE_NUMBER, FILES
- SELECT('opt':color, ...) / MULTI_SELECT('opt':color, ...)
- Option names can't contain commas: use '$1000+', not '$1,000+'. List separate options as 'A', 'B', not 'A, B'.
- STATUS('Backlog':gray:to_do, 'Building':blue:in_progress, 'Shipped':green:complete); groups are to_do, in_progress, complete
- NUMBER [FORMAT 'dollar'] / FORMULA('expression')
- RELATION('ds') for a one-way relation
- RELATION('ds', DUAL) for a two-way relation
- RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children') with a synced property name
- RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children' 'children') with a synced name and synced_id (for self-relations)
- ROLLUP('rel_prop', 'target_prop', 'function')
- UNIQUE_ID [PREFIX 'WEB-BUG'] / CREATED_TIME / LAST_EDITED_TIME
- UNIQUE_ID PREFIX: 2-10 characters, a letter then letters, digits, or hyphens (e.g. 'TASK-ID', not 'TASK_ID' or 'T'). Each prefix can be used by only one data source per workspace, so prefer a specific prefix like 'WEB-BUG' over 'TASK'.
- Any column: COMMENT 'description text' Colors: default, gray, brown, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, red.


Examples:
- <example>ADD COLUMN "Priority" SELECT('High':red, 'Medium':yellow, 'Low':green); ADD COLUMN "Due Date" DATE</example>
- <example>RENAME COLUMN "Status" TO "Project Status"</example>
- <example>DROP COLUMN "Old Property"</example>
- For a self-relation, add both relation properties in one call with matching DUAL names and IDs, such as <example>ADD COLUMN "Parent" RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children' 'children')</example>.

title.description: The new title of the data source.

description.description: The new description of the data source.

is_inline.description: Whether the database should display inline (true) or as full page (false). Only applicable for single-source databases.

in_trash.description: Move data source to trash. Cannot be undone without Notion UI.

page_layout.description: Replaces the data source's page layout. Refer to existing properties by name. See notion://docs/database-page-layouts. Example: <example>{"main":[{"type":"title","pinnedProperties":["Status","Owner"]},{"type":"editor"},{"type":"discussions"}],"sidebar":[{"type":"properties"}]}</example>.

pinnedProperties.description: Property names to show under the title.

propertyLabels.description: Whether pinned properties show their names.

relation.description: The name of a two-way relation property whose related pages show as a view.

main.description: Main area modules in order. Include a title, an editor (unless the layout has a tab), and discussions.

sidebar.description: Sidebar modules in order. Only properties and property modules are allowed.

tab.description: Puts page content in a tab next to database views. Omit for a simple layout.

id.description: The existing tab ID from fetch. Omit for a new tab. Starts with view_tab_.

modules.description: Tab modules in order. Must include an editor. Only properties, property modules, discussions, relations, and the editor are allowed.

propertyIcons.description: Whether property icons show on the page.

pageFullWidth.description: Whether pages open at full width.

instructions_version.description: Notion setup instructions version, such as 0.0.2. Omit if unknown.

skill.description: For tracking only: the name of the agent skill you are following for this task, such as notion-meeting-prep. Omit if you are not following a skill.

properties.description: Properties in order. Unlisted properties follow in their current order and show. Don't list the title or properties placed elsewhere in the layout.

visibility.description: Defaults to show. Changes how pages look, not who can see the value.

properties.description: Properties in this section, in order. Don't list the title or properties placed elsewhere in the layout.

sections.description: Named sections in order. Unlisted properties go in the last section and show.

property.description: The name of the property to show.

style.description: Display style. Which styles apply depends on the property type.

tools.name: notion-update-page
tools.description: Update a Notion page's properties, content, icon, or cover. For only an icon or cover, use "update_properties" without "properties". ## Core rules **IMPORTANT**: Before writing page content, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-rea...

page_id.description: The page ID, with or without dashes, or a Notion page URL.

properties.description:
Used by the "update_properties" command, and required unless "icon", "cover", "is_skill", or "full_width" is set. A JSON object that updates the page's properties.
For pages in a database, fetch the page or its data source first and use the exact property names and SQLite schema definition shown in <database>.
For page titles outside a database, use "title" in inline Markdown.
For a Files property, an uploaded file can be provided as {"type":"file_upload","file_upload":{"id":"<file-upload-id>"}} inside the property's array.
Use null to remove a property's value.
**IMPORTANT**: Some property types require specific formats:
- Date properties: Split into "date:{property}:start", "date:{property}:end" (optional), and "date:{property}:is_datetime" (0 or 1)
- Place properties: Split into "place:{property}:name", "place:{property}:address", "place:{property}:latitude", "place:{property}:longitude", and "place:{property}:google_place_id" (optional)
- Number properties: Use JavaScript numbers (not strings)
- Checkbox properties: Use "__YES__" for checked, "__NO__" for unchecked
- Relation properties: Use an array of related page URLs or page IDs, e.g. ["https://www.notion.so/26ab1f9f4c5f80b18d3bd10a6b1d2f4e", "26ab1f9f-4c5f-80b1-8d3b-d10a6b1d2f4e"]
- Person properties: Use an array of user IDs, user or agent URLs, or group references copied from fetch output ("space_permission_group-<UUID>"). Bare group UUIDs are also supported.
- Files properties: Use a JSON array of file IDs, Notion Folder URLs, and/or <folder> tags copied from fetch output. Folders are stored as native Folder references, not ordinary links.


**Special property naming**: Properties named "id" or "url" (case insensitive) must be prefixed with "userDefined:" (e.g., "userDefined:URL", "userDefined:id")

id.description: ID of a file upload returned by create_file_upload or create_attachment.

file_upload.description: The uploaded file to attach to the Files property.

full_width.description: With command update_properties, set a page to full width or the default width. For database pages, overrides the database layout for this page only.

new_str.description: Required for "replace_content" command. The new content string to replace the entire page content with. Preserve child pages and databases with their exact fetched <page url="..."> or <database url="..."> tags. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

content.description: Required for "insert_content" command. The markdown content to insert into the page. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

content_updates.description: Required for "update_content" command. An array of search-and-replace operations, each with old_str (content to find) and new_str (replacement content). Operations that match are applied, and each one that matches nothing is reported in "warnings". The call fails only when no operation that changes content matches.

old_str.description: The existing content string to find and replace. Must exactly match the page content.

new_str.description: The new content string to replace old_str with. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

replace_all_matches.description: If true, replaces all occurrences of old_str. If false (default), the operation fails if there are multiple matches.

position.description: Optional for "insert_content" command. Use {"type":"start"} to prepend content or {"type":"end"} to append content. Omit to append.

type.description: Insert the content at the start of the page.
Insert the content at the end of the page.

allow_deleting_content.description: Optional for "replace_content" and "update_content" commands. Set to true to allow deletion of child pages and databases that are not referenced in the new content. If false or omitted, the operation will fail with an error listing the pages/databases that would be deleted. Show that list and ask the user for confirmation before retrying with true.

template_id.description: Required for "apply_template" command. The ID of a template to apply to this page; any page ID can be used as a template. Template content is appended to any existing page content asynchronously.

verification_status.description: Required for "update_verification" command. Set to "verified" to mark the page as verified, or "unverified" to remove verification. Requires a Business or Enterprise plan unless the page is in a wiki. When updating verification, the owner will be automatically set to the authenticated actor.

verification_expiry_days.description: Optional for "update_verification" command when verification_status is "verified". Number of days until verification expires (e.g. 7, 30, 90). Omit for indefinite verification.

icon.description: An emoji character (e.g. "🚀"), a custom emoji by name (e.g. ":rocket_ship:"), a Notion icon identifier as returned by fetch (e.g. "icons/pizza_blue"), or an external image URL. Use "none" to remove the icon. Omit to leave unchanged. Can be set alongside any command. To change only the icon, use "update_properties" and omit "properties". Keep the title free of a duplicate leading emoji because the icon renders separately.

cover.description: An external image URL for the page cover. Use "none" to remove the cover. Omit to leave unchanged. Can be set alongside any command. To change only the cover, use "update_properties" and omit "properties".

is_skill.description: Set to true to mark this page as a skill, or false to remove the skill designation. Can be set alongside any command. To change only skill status, use "update_properties" and omit "properties". Before creating a skill, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/skills` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface. If your client does not support reading MCP resources, call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI instead. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool.

allow_async.description: Default to true for page updates. Set to false only when the next step needs the updated page immediately, or when async execution rejects the request as too large. When this update operation is accepted for background execution, it returns an async_task result. Use get_async_task to wait for a succeeded status before taking a dependent action on the page. For apply_template, a succeeded status does not mean template content is ready; fetch and retry until it is ready before changing or relying on that content. If omitted or false, the tool waits for a synchronous result when possible, but may still return a pollable async_task response if queued execution exceeds the synchronous wait deadline.

instructions_version.description: Notion setup instructions version, such as 0.0.2. Omit if unknown.

skill.description: For tracking only: the name of the agent skill you are following for this task, such as notion-meeting-prep. Omit if you are not following a skill.
